quote: Oh, wow. Yeah. That is that's pretty expensive.
stewart_read: Rep acknowledges the $400 bill emotionally but never flips it into a reason-to-act line (e.g., tying it forward to the appointment or the utility company as the real cost). Capture without flip.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to follow acknowledgment with a forward-pulling line, e.g., tying the $400 to what the appointment will show him he could save, per coaching_philosophy.bill_anchoring's 'ask + acknowledge + flip' pattern.

quote: I'm not at home. I'm at work. I'd like to meet me at work if if you guys wanna come see me, give you my work address.
stewart_read: A real logistical constraint (customer's location) derails the standard bill-collection and appointment flow. The rep never firmly resolves whether the visit happens at home or work before offering a time.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: the rep is just handling a genuine curveball in real time with no script for it. Strategic: unlikely — there's no evidence the rep is deliberately deferring to set up a stronger later move; the manager-check line at 05:09 reads as genuine uncertainty, not a planned tactic.
coaching_implication: This should be flagged as a fragile/conditional booking in the handoff — the closer needs to know the venue isn't locked.

quote: Is there any way you could send it before? It just helps us to build it up for you. No.
stewart_read: This is a rep line followed immediately by the customer's one-word decline — the rep made a third attempt to get the bill sooner and the customer shut it down flatly. The thread ends here without an agreed method or deadline.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close this loop with a specific commitment ('I'll text you a link right now, and if you can send it back by end of day that would be ideal') rather than letting a flat 'no' end the thread.

quote: Gotcha. I mean, we we I think we'd prefer to come to the house just if that work for you, we could do it when you when do you do it at home. No.
stewart_read: The rep tries once to steer back to a home visit but immediately folds when the customer says no, without exploring alternatives like a phone appointment (Ion's stated standard model) instead of an in-person visit at either location.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: rep lacks a scripted fallback for 'customer wants in-person at work' and defaults to accepting the work address. Strategic read doesn't hold — there's no indication this ambiguity serves a later close; it just leaves the appointment mechanics unresolved.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to consider offering the standard phone-based design review as a fallback when in-person logistics get complicated, since Ion's model per the schema is a phone appointment with a closer, not necessarily a field visit.
